awd_titl_txt: Conference: Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics at Penn State
awd_abstract_narration:
This award provides funding for participants in “Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics at Penn State,” to be held on the Penn State University Park campus November 13-16, 2025.  This represents the Penn State half of the Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics, cosponsored for the last 35 years by the dynamics groups of Penn State and University of Maryland; the Maryland half is held each spring. The workshop is devoted to recent developments in dynamical systems and many applications to related fields.  The goals of this conference are to promote the communication of mathematical results, to facilitate interaction and progress in dynamical systems and related fields, to nurture the sense of community and common mission in these fields, and to contribute to the training of graduate students and recent Ph.D. recipients and to their integration into the dynamics community. 

This conference series began as a meeting place for mathematicians based primarily in the northeastern United States working in dynamical systems and related topics, and during the past twenty years has grown to attract outstanding mathematicians from around the world.  In recent years the conference has featured several special sessions focused on the latest achievements and current research trends in dynamics and its applications.  The themes for the 2025 edition of the workshop include classification of measures for homogeneous and non-homogeneous systems, ergodic and mixing properties of parabolic flows and sharp bounds on their deviation of ergodic averages, new developments for random systems, recent trends in the theory of Hamiltonian dynamics, statistical properties of non-uniformly hyperbolic systems and their thermodynamic formalism. More information can be found on the conference website at https://science.psu.edu/math/research/dynsys/workshop.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Intellectual merit.

The Fall Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics at Penn State is one of two complementary semi-annual meetings organized with the dynamics group at the University of Maryland, College Park. The Penn State workshop has been held each fall since 1990; the Maryland meeting began in 1992. Together they are among the leading U.S. conferences in dynamical systems, bringing together senior researchers, early-career mathematicians, postdoctoral fellows, and graduate students to present current work across a broad range of topics.

The 36th Workshop was held November 13 - 16, 2025. Speakers during the award period included V. Climenhaga, M. Foreman, G. Forni, M. Gerber, H. Hofer, P. Kunde, M. Leguil, H. Oh, M. Sabok, R. Sharp, K. Simon, R. Spatzier, C. Ulcigrai, and K. Vinhage, in addition to members of the Penn State and Maryland groups. Program highlights included a special session on anti-classification results in dynamics and smooth manifolds; the 14th Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems, awarded on November 15 to Dan Cristofaro-Gardiner, with talks by Helmut Hofer and Bassam Fayad on the prize-winning work; and book exhibits by the American Mathematical Society, Cambridge University Press, World Scientific, and the University of Chicago Press.

Broader impacts.

NSF support for this award has made the workshop accessible to early-career researchers and has raised the visibility of dynamical systems. Graduate students and postdoctoral researchers comprised 73% of participants and had dedicated speaking slots and poster sessions. Lodging subsidies for attendees and travel support for those with financial need allowed many early-career dynamicists to attend and present their work.

The workshop also hosted the Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems. The associated ceremony and invited talks provided public recognition and visible role models for younger researchers, helped motivate high-quality work, and strengthened the workshop as a national venue for both scientific exchange and community building.
